projects.ai-order-cloud.headline: Designing AI around the work—not the novelty.
projects.product-page-architecture.role: As the sole designer on this initiative, I helped diagnose the experience, synthesized behavioral and market evidence, proposed the new information architecture, and carried the direction through design exploration, prototyping, usability testing, and an A/B test.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.headlin: Powerful features for admins. Effortless engagement for everyone else.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.heading: Why it mattered.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.context: Recognition was one of our most-requested features and a natural extension of BambooHR’s “better together” story. As the first HRIS to offer it natively, our goal went beyond competitive parity: create an exceptional experience for admins and employees.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.adminCh: I couldn’t remove all of the complexity from the admin experience, but I could make it easier to navigate. I organized the system around clear decisions, introduced complexity only when it was needed, and showed admins what would happen before they committed to a change.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.problem: Recognition & Rewards had to serve two very different jobs. Admins needed control over eligibility, points, rewards, and automation. Employees needed a fast, natural way to recognize someone. The challenge was to minimize complexity on the admin side and remove friction from the employee side.
about.body: I have a pragmatic approach to design—focus on human-centered design principles and results that drive business outcomes. Outside of work, I’m usually spending time with my family and our dogs. I love the desert, photography, and tinkering with 3D modeling/ printing. More than anything, I like making things. I’ve been fascinated by how things work for as long as I can remember, and few things are more satisfying than repairing something that would otherwise end up in the trash.
projects.recognition-and-rewards.outcome: Post-launch customer conversations also led us to ship more granular point allocations and automated birthday and anniversary recognition.
projects.product-page-architecture.draft: After roughly four weeks live, the results confirmed the hypothesis: customers didn't need fewer opportunities; they just needed them in the right order.

After a redesign by an external agency, upgrades and cross-sells had flattened. Site data showed the decline, but not the cause. I paired quantitative data with user sessions and heat maps from Quantum Metric. The synthesis revealed a clear pattern of hesitation and second guessing with each additional decision we put on the PDP.
Site data showed the decline. Research showed us why.
Our competitors repeated the same mistake.

We audited competitors in and out of market. Most in-category experiences stacked every cross-sell in the PDP, repeating the same overloaded pattern. Looking elsewhere surfaced stronger ways to sequence configuration and add-on decisions.
projects.ai-order-cloud.approach.0.body: I brought executives, department leaders, and key stakeholders together to identify where AI could create credible customer and business value. The workshop gave design a strategic role early enough to influence the premise, not just the interface.

projects.product-page-architecture.draft: Keep momentum without removing the choices.
Every offer competed with the primary job to be done.

We launched the A/B test with only 10% of traffic to the new experience, then 50% and finally 100%. After four weeks live, the results confirmed our hypothesis: customers didn't need fewer choices; they just needed them in the right order.
